summary: legal checked in 4 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: Recommendation: keep SearchWoot private and keep external outreach unsent. Official Woot documentation establishes API access mechanics, not public or commercial reuse rights; all four legal checklist tasks remain open. Smallest next step: complete the consolidated rights, data-flow, consent, vendor, retention, and incident evidence bundle, then route it for human-counsel review. Owner authorization remains required before any permission request is sent.

Risk disposition: blocked for public launch of the gated product; conditional for ordinary reversible fleet growth; counsel_required for upstream data rights, jurisdiction-specific privacy treatment, vendor/DPA obligations, and future affiliate or advertising use. Exact decision: keep the gated product private and keep external outreach unsent. Evidence: official API documentation confirms access mechanics but not rights to store, transform, cache, display, retain historical derivatives, send alerts, use images/trademarks/prices, or monetize returned data; current public terms point against the proposed commercial/public use. Compliance baseline is technical only: 35 pass, 14 fail, 10 unknown, with open banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings. Analytics is configured for 39 sites but has source-permission errors; this is not a general growth blocker. Revenue covers 2026-09-21 only: 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 aggregate commission; the aggregate row is not site-attributable, so ROI and site economics remain unsupported. Fleet security, operations, accuracy/freshness, attribution, and measurement gates remain incomplete. Ordinary reversible growth may continue only where existing consent, disclosures, provenance, claims, affiliate, platform-policy, and data-handling boundaries are preserved.

Launch-readiness tracking remains active. Progress: 0 of 4 legal tasks closed; no task has sufficient evidence for closure. Open tasks are source rights, alert-data flow and retention, GA4 consent/configuration, and logs/vendors/incident handling. Existing evidence is partial: official source documentation and terms, repository/configuration data-flow files, privacy and cookie pages, and draft terms are present, but none establish complete launch readiness. Next evidence action: attach one consolidated read-only bundle and field-level rights matrix covering source provenance, permitted storage/display/alerts, freshness, correction, takedown, identifiers, retention, deletion, access, notification consent, unsubscribe behavior, GA4 settings, log fields, vendor/DPA coverage, and incident/request procedures. Do not send outreach, change the private gate, enable tracking, or expand monetization.

Data-use review: Woot API deal and price-history data = counsel_required and launch-blocked. Missing current written permission or API agreement, field-level provenance and rights, permitted caching/display/alert terms, attribution, freshness, correction, takedown, trademark/image/price limits, and affiliate or advertising terms. Smallest next action: complete the field-level rights matrix and route the unsent permission package for human-counsel review. User alert rules and sync results = evidence_needed. Missing data inventory, identifiers, retention, deletion, correction, access, processor terms, notification consent, and unsubscribe behavior. Smallest next action: produce the repository and deployed data-flow and retention table. GA4 analytics = evidence_needed. Missing deployed consent and withdrawal behavior, GA4 property/data-sharing settings, retention settings, and jurisdictional privacy review. Smallest next action: capture existing consent and GA4 configuration without enabling tracking. Operational logs and Cloudflare hosting data = evidence_needed. Missing log-field inventory, retention/access controls, vendor/DPA review, and incident/request procedures. Smallest next action: produce a read-only operator and vendor inventory and identify counsel-required gaps.
